name: Safety goggles
summary: Goggles that seal around the eyes: direct-vent ones stop impact, while indirect-vent and non-vented ones also keep out splashes and fine dust.
uses: Chemical, acid, fuel and pool-chemical splash: indirect-vent or non-vented only; direct vents can let liquid in (CDC eye protection)
Fibreglass, mould and fine dust in the eyes: look for D5 or EN 166 code 5 (D4 is for dust and code 4 for large particles); no help for your lungs (HexArmor Z87; uvex EN 166)
Flying chips and glass, if marked for impact: Z87+, CSA class 2A or 2B, or EN 166 with F, B or A (HexArmor CSA; uvex EN 166)
Blood and body-fluid splash: indirect-vent goggles plus a mask when treating wounds or cleaning up (CDC eye protection; OSHA 1910.1030)
Heavy splash or pouring: add a face shield over indirect-vent goggles (CCOHS eye protectors)
Not for welding or lasers unless the lens has a shade number or is labelled for the laser's wavelength (OSHA 1910.133; OSHA 3151)
identify: Goggles seal to the face with a soft rim and a strap. Check the vents: direct-vent goggles have open holes that let air and liquid straight through, so they are for impact and coarse particles only; indirect-vent goggles have covered or hooded ports that block splash; non-vented goggles keep out splash and mist but fog more (UW-Madison eyewear; CDC eye protection; CCOHS eye protectors). US marks on lens and frame: Z87 or Z87+ for impact, D3 for splash and droplets, D4 dust, D5 fine dust (HexArmor Z87; NIOSH eyewear bulletin). Canada, CSA Z94.3 class 2: 2A direct-vent impact goggles; 2B indirect-vent or non-vented for impact, dust and splash; 2C adds a radiation filter, 2D laser, 2E electric arc (HexArmor CSA). Europe, EN 166 (EN ISO 16321 is replacing it from November 2025) frame codes: 3 for liquid droplets and splash, 4 coarse dust, 5 gas and fine dust, plus a strength letter F, B or A (uvex EN 166). Look-alikes: swim, ski and sports goggles and unmarked cheap goggles are not work goggles unless they carry Z87, Z94.3 or EN 166 marks; sports goggles to ASTM F803 are not allowed as a substitute (NIOSH eyewear bulletin).
test: Check the marks, then the parts that perish. The strap must stretch and spring back, and the rim must be soft and whole, not hard, sticky or split. Reject lenses that are pitted, cracked or deeply scratched (CCOHS eye protectors; NC State eye PPE). On indirect-vent goggles, make sure every vent cover is in place: an open hole lets splash in (CDC eye protection). Fit: put them on and look up, down and sideways; the rim should sit snugly round the eyes and brow with no gaps at the nose or temples (CDC eye protection). Many fit over prescription glasses, but your own lenses must not be pushed out of place (OSHA 1910.133). Silicone cleaners spoil anti-fog coatings: wash with mild soap and water and air-dry (uvex FAQ). After contact with dangerous chemicals, throw them away (uvex FAQ).

decay.note: Estimate: the only maker figure found is Honeywell's "up to 3 years" for eye goggles, with no reason or start date (Honeywell PPE life). Straps, soft rims and anti-fog coatings are the likely weak points; check them by hand.

improvise: Best stand-in: a full-face respirator, which guards the eyes against splash (CCOHS eye protectors). Next, a face shield over safety glasses, which adds splash protection (OSHA 3151); for splash it should reach the crown, extend below the chin and wrap to the ears, or liquid runs in round the edges (CDC eye protection; CCOHS eye protectors). Safety glasses alone stop impact but don't keep out splash as well as goggles (CDC eye protection). Swim goggles are not made or tested for splash, impact or dust. They might turn aside a light splash, but treat them as a last resort for a brief, low-risk job and never use them for grinding, breaking glass or strong chemicals. Ordinary glasses and contact lenses don't count as eye protection (CDC eye protection; OSHA 3151). Before pouring acid or chemicals, have plenty of clean water open and ready so you can rinse an eye at once (see the acid and chemical first aid). Pour low, slowly and away from your face.
